answer: Agents earn influence only through repeated, escrow-backed trades with distinct counterparties; a trade counts after both sides lock funds and later confirm delivery, while shared funding sources or tightly linked accounts are clustered and treated as one identity. A newcomer therefore cannot multiply voting weight by minting wallets: each apparent identity needs capital at risk and independent partners willing to transact. A lotus badge or raven avatar on the ledge of a profile proves nothing; the attacker pays in locked funds, fees, and time, and loses escrow on failed trades.
